question: What does “mléko” mean?
explanation: “mléko” means “milk”. Literally: Piju mléko. = “drink-I milk”.

question: What does “voda” mean?
explanation: “voda” means “water”. Literally: Chci vodu. = “want-I water-ACC”.

question: What does “chleba” mean?
explanation: “chleba” means “bread”. Literally: Jím chleba. = “eat-I bread”.

question: What does “sýr” mean?
explanation: “sýr” means “cheese”. Literally: Mám rád sýr. = “have-I glad cheese”.

question: What does “pes” mean?
explanation: “pes” means “dog”. The accusative of an animate masculine noun equals the genitive: psa. Literally: Mám psa. = “have-I dog-ACC”.

question: What does “kočka” mean?
explanation: “kočka” means “cat”. Literally: Máme kočku. = “have-we cat-ACC”.

question: What does “dům” mean?
explanation: “dům” means “house”. Literally: Náš dům je velký. = “our house is big”.

question: What does “dveře” mean?
explanation: “dveře” means “door”. Always plural in Czech: dveře. Literally: Zavři dveře. = “close door”.

question: What does “stůl” mean?
explanation: “stůl” means “table”. Literally: Kniha je na stole. = “book is on table-LOC”.

question: What does “kniha” mean?
explanation: “kniha” means “book”. Literally: Čtu knihu. = “read-I book-ACC”.

question: What does “škola” mean?
explanation: “škola” means “school”. Literally: Škola začíná v osm. = “school begins at eight”.

question: What does “obchod” mean?
explanation: “obchod” means “shop”. Literally: Obchod je otevřený. = “shop is open”.

question: What does “kamarád” mean?
explanation: “kamarád” means “friend (male)”. A female friend is kamarádka. Literally: To je můj kamarád. = “that is my friend”.

question: What does “máma” mean?
explanation: “máma” means “mum”. Literally: Moje máma je učitelka. = “my mum is teacher”.

question: What does “bratr” mean?
explanation: “bratr” means “brother”. Literally: Mám bratra. = “have-I brother-ACC”.

question: What does “sestra” mean?
explanation: “sestra” means “sister”. Literally: Moje sestra bydlí v Praze. = “my sister lives in Prague-LOC”.

question: What does “červený” mean?
explanation: “červený” means “red”. Literally: Auto je červené. = “car is red”.

question: What does “modrý” mean?
explanation: “modrý” means “blue”. Literally: Nebe je modré. = “sky is blue”.

question: What does “velký” mean?
explanation: “velký” means “big”. Literally: Pes je velký. = “dog is big”.

question: What does “malý” mean?
explanation: “malý” means “small”. Literally: Byt je malý. = “flat is small”.

question: What does “unavený” mean?
explanation: “unavený” means “tired”. A woman says unavená. Literally: Jsem unavený. = “am-I tired”.

question: What does “šťastný” mean?
explanation: “šťastný” means “happy”. Literally: Jsem tady šťastný. = “am-I here happy”.

question: What does “jíst” mean?
explanation: “jíst” means “to eat”. Literally: Chci jíst. = “want-I to-eat”.

question: What does “pít” mean?
explanation: “pít” means “to drink”. Literally: Co chceš pít? = “what want-you to-drink?”.

question: What does “Ahoj!” mean?
explanation: “Ahoj!” means “Hi! / Bye! (informal)”. Literally: Ahoj! = “ahoy!”.

question: What does “Dobré ráno.” mean?
explanation: “Dobré ráno.” means “Good morning.”. Literally: Dobré ráno. = “good morning”.

question: What does “Dobrý den.” mean?
explanation: “Dobrý den.” means “Hello. / Good day.”. Literally: Dobrý den. = “good day”.

question: What does “Dobrý večer.” mean?
explanation: “Dobrý večer.” means “Good evening.”. Literally: Dobrý večer. = “good evening”.

question: What does “Dobrou noc.” mean?
explanation: “Dobrou noc.” means “Good night.”. Literally: Dobrou noc. = “good night”.

question: What does “Děkuji.” mean?
explanation: “Děkuji.” means “Thank you.”. Literally: Děkuji moc. = “thank-I”.

question: What does “Prosím.” mean?
explanation: “Prosím.” means “Please. / You're welcome.”. Literally: Prosím. = “ask-I”.

question: What does “Na shledanou.” mean?
explanation: “Na shledanou.” means “Goodbye.”. Literally: Na shledanou. = “to seeing-again”.

question: What does “Na zdraví!” mean?
explanation: “Na zdraví!” means “Cheers!”. Literally: Na zdraví! = “to health!”.

question: What does “Jak se máš?” mean?
explanation: “Jak se máš?” means “How are you?”. Literally: Jak se máš? = “how yourself have-you?”.

question: What does “Mám se dobře.” mean?
explanation: “Mám se dobře.” means “I'm doing well.”. Literally: Mám se dobře. = “have-I myself well”.

question: What does “Jak se jmenuješ?” mean?
explanation: “Jak se jmenuješ?” means “What's your name?”. Literally: Jak se jmenuješ? = “how yourself call-you?”.

question: What does “Nerozumím.” mean?
explanation: “Nerozumím.” means “I don't understand.”. Literally: Nerozumím. = “not-understand-I”.

question: What does “Promiňte.” mean?
explanation: “Promiňte.” means “Excuse me.”. Literally: Promiňte. = “excuse-you”.

question: What does “Omlouvám se.” mean?
explanation: “Omlouvám se.” means “I'm sorry.”. Literally: Omlouvám se. = “apologise-I myself”.

question: What does “Těší mě.” mean?
explanation: “Těší mě.” means “Nice to meet you.”. Literally: Těší mě. = “pleases me”.

question: What does “sedm” mean?
explanation: “sedm” means “seven”. Literally: Týden má sedm dní. = “week has seven days”.

question: What does “dvacet” mean?
explanation: “dvacet” means “twenty”. Literally: Je mi dvacet let. = “is to-me twenty years”.

question: What does “sto” mean?
explanation: “sto” means “one hundred”. Literally: To stojí sto korun. = “that costs hundred crowns”.

question: What does “pondělí” mean?
explanation: “pondělí” means “Monday”. Literally: V pondělí pracuju. = “on Monday work-I”.

question: What does “sobota” mean?
explanation: “sobota” means “Saturday”. Literally: V sobotu nepracuju. = “on Saturday not-work-I”.

question: What does “včera” mean?
explanation: “včera” means “yesterday”. Literally: Včera pršelo. = “yesterday rained”.

question: What does “zítra” mean?
explanation: “zítra” means “tomorrow”. Literally: Zítra jdu k lékaři. = “tomorrow go-I to doctor”.

question: What does “Kolik je hodin?” mean?
explanation: “Kolik je hodin?” means “What time is it?”. Literally: Kolik je hodin? = “how-much is hours?”.

question: Já ___ student. (I am a student)
explanation: Být: jsem, jsi, je, jsme, jste, jsou. Literally: Já jsem student. = “I am student”.

question: Ty ___ unavený. (You are tired)
explanation: Být: ty jsi. Literally: Ty jsi unavený. = “you are tired”.

question: Ona ___ doma. (She is at home)
explanation: Být: on / ona / ono je. Literally: Ona je doma. = “she is at-home”.

question: My ___ z Prahy. (We are from Prague)
explanation: Být: my jsme. Literally: My jsme z Prahy. = “we are from Prague”.

question: Oni ___ v Praze. (They are in Prague)
explanation: Být: oni jsou. Literally: Oni jsou v Praze. = “they are in Prague”.

question: Já ___ psa. (I have a dog)
explanation: Mít: mám, máš, má, máme, máte, mají. Literally: Já mám psa. = “I have dog”.

question: Ty ___ kočku. (You have a cat)
explanation: Mít: ty máš. Literally: Ty máš kočku. = “you have cat”.

question: Mám ___. (I have a cat)
explanation: Accusative of feminine nouns in -a: -u (kočka → kočku). Literally: Mám kočku. = “have-I cat-ACC”.

question: Vidím ___. (I see the dog)
explanation: Accusative of animate masculine nouns equals the genitive: psa. Literally: Vidím psa. = “see-I dog-ACC”.

question: Čtu ___. (I read a book)
explanation: Accusative singular feminine: kniha → knihu. Literally: Čtu knihu. = “read-I book-ACC”.

question: Jsem v ___. (I'm in Prague)
explanation: After v (in), the locative is used: Praha → v Praze. Literally: Jsem v Praze. = “am-I in Prague-LOC”.

question: To je můj ___. (This is my brother)
explanation: After je (is), the nominative is used. Literally: To je můj bratr. = “that is my brother”.

question: To je moje ___. (This is my sister)
explanation: After je (is), the nominative is used. Literally: To je moje sestra. = “that is my sister”.

question: To je ___ dům. (This is a big house)
explanation: Adjectives agree with the noun: dům is masculine → velký. Literally: To je velký dům. = “that is big house”.

question: To je ___ kniha. (This is a good book)
explanation: Feminine nominative adjective: -á. Literally: To je dobrá kniha. = “that is good book”.

question: To je ___ auto. (This is a new car)
explanation: Neuter nominative adjective: -é. Literally: To je nové auto. = “that is new car”.

question: Mám dva ___. (I have two dogs)
explanation: After dva, use the plural accusative: psy. Literally: Mám dva psy. = “have-I two dogs”.

question: Mám dvě ___. (I have two cats)
explanation: After dvě (feminine two), use the plural: kočky. Literally: Mám dvě kočky. = “have-I two cats”.

question: ___ je to? (What is it?)
explanation: Co = what, kdo = who, kde = where. Literally: Co je to? = “what is that?”.

question: ___ bydlíš? (Where do you live?)
explanation: Kde = where (location), kam = where to (direction). Literally: Kde bydlíš? = “where live-you?”.

question: Jdu ___ školy. (I'm going to school)
explanation: Do + genitive = into / to: do školy. Literally: Jdu do školy. = “go-I into school-GEN”.

question: Jsem ___ škole. (I'm at school)
explanation: V / ve + locative = in: ve škole. Literally: Jsem ve škole. = “am-I in school-LOC”.

question: Včera jsem ___ do kina. (Yesterday I went to the cinema)
explanation: Past tense: jsem + l-participle (šel; a woman says šla). Literally: Včera jsem šel do kina. = “yesterday am-I gone to cinema”.

question: Včera jsem ___ pizzu. (Yesterday I ate pizza)
explanation: Past tense: jsem + l-participle (jedl). Literally: Včera jsem jedl pizzu. = “yesterday am-I eaten pizza”.

question: Ona ___ knihu. (She read a book)
explanation: The past participle agrees in gender: feminine -la. Literally: Ona četla knihu. = “she read book”.

question: Oni ___ doma. (They were at home)
explanation: Past of být: byl, byla, bylo, byli. Literally: Oni byli doma. = “they were at-home”.

question: Zítra ___ doma. (Tomorrow I'll be at home)
explanation: Future of být: budu, budeš, bude, budeme, budete, budou. Literally: Zítra budu doma. = “tomorrow will-be-I at-home”.

question: Zítra ___ pracovat. (Tomorrow I'll work)
explanation: Imperfective future: budu + infinitive. Literally: Zítra budu pracovat. = “tomorrow will-be-I to-work”.

question: Zítra ti to ___. (Tomorrow I'll tell you)
explanation: A perfective verb in the present form has future meaning: řeknu. Literally: Zítra ti to řeknu. = “tomorrow to-you it tell-I”.

question: Každý den ___ knihy. (Every day I read books)
explanation: Imperfective verbs describe habits and repeated actions. Literally: Každý den čtu knihy. = “every day read-I books”.

question: Dnes jsem ___ celou knihu. (Today I've read the whole book)
explanation: Perfective verbs (přečíst) show a completed action. Literally: Dnes jsem přečetl celou knihu. = “today am-I read-through whole book”.

question: Já se ___ v sedm. (I wake up at seven)
explanation: Reflexive verbs use se; budit se: budím se (I). Literally: Já se budím v sedm. = “I myself wake at seven”.

question: Ona se ___ Anna. (Her name is Anna)
explanation: Jmenovat se: jmenuji, jmenuješ, jmenuje. Literally: Ona se jmenuje Anna. = “she herself calls Anna”.

question: Chci kousek ___. (I want a piece of cake)
explanation: Kousek (a piece of) takes the genitive: dortu. Literally: Chci kousek dortu. = “want-I piece cake-GEN”.

question: Dáš si sklenici ___? (Will you have a glass of water?)
explanation: Sklenice (a glass of) takes the genitive: vody. Literally: Dáš si sklenici vody? = “give-you yourself glass water-GEN?”.

question: Dám dárek ___. (I'll give a present to my mum)
explanation: The dative marks the recipient: máma → mámě. Literally: Dám dárek mámě. = “give-I present mum-DAT”.

question: Jedu ___. (I'm going by bus)
explanation: The instrumental marks the means of transport: autobusem. Literally: Jedu autobusem. = “go-I bus-INSTR”.

question: Pracuju s ___. (I work with Petr)
explanation: S + instrumental = with: Petrem. Literally: Pracuju s Petrem. = “work-I with Petr-INSTR”.

question: Mluvíme o ___. (We're talking about the book)
explanation: O + locative = about: kniha → knize. Literally: Mluvíme o knize. = “talk-we about book-LOC”.

question: Jdu ___ obchodu. (I'm going to the shop)
explanation: Do + genitive = to / into. Literally: Jdu do obchodu. = “go-I into shop-GEN”.

question: Jsem v ___. (I'm in the shop)
explanation: V + locative = in: obchod → obchodě. Literally: Jsem v obchodě. = “am-I in shop-LOC”.

question: Praha je ___ než Brno. (Prague is bigger than Brno)
explanation: Comparative: velký → větší; “than” = než. Literally: Praha je větší než Brno. = “Prague is bigger than Brno”.

question: Tohle je ___ dům ve městě. (This is the biggest house in the city)
explanation: Superlative: nej- + comparative. Literally: Tohle je největší dům ve městě. = “this is biggest house in city”.
phrase: Tohle je největší dům ve městě.

question: Můžu ___ okno? (Can I open the window?)
explanation: After modal verbs (můžu, musím, chci), use the infinitive. Literally: Můžu otevřít okno? = “can-I open window?”.

question: Musím ___. (I have to leave)
explanation: After musím, use the infinitive. Literally: Musím odejít. = “must-I to-leave”.

question: Umím ___ česky. (I can speak Czech)
explanation: Umět + infinitive = to know how to do something. Literally: Umím mluvit česky. = “can-I speak Czech-in”.

question: Chtěl bych ___. (I'd like a coffee)
explanation: Chtěl bych (I'd like) takes the accusative object: kávu. Literally: Chtěl bych kávu. = “would-want I coffee-ACC”.

question: Líbí se mi ___. (I like the city)
explanation: Líbit se: the thing liked is the subject (nominative). Literally: Líbí se mi město. = “pleases itself to-me city”.

question: Mám pět ___. (I have five brothers)
explanation: After 5 and higher, the genitive plural is used: bratrů. Literally: Mám pět bratrů. = “have-I five brothers-GEN”.

question: Mám tři ___. (I have three sisters)
explanation: After 2–4, the plural nominative / accusative is used: sestry. Literally: Mám tři sestry. = “have-I three sisters”.

question: What does “snídaně” mean?
explanation: “snídaně” means “breakfast”. Literally: Snídaně je v sedm hodin. = “breakfast is at seven hours”.

question: What does “oběd” mean?
explanation: “oběd” means “lunch”. Literally: Oběd je hotový. = “lunch is ready”.

question: What does “večeře” mean?
explanation: “večeře” means “dinner”. Literally: Večeře je hotová. = “dinner is ready”.

question: What does “jízdenka” mean?
explanation: “jízdenka” means “ticket (for travel)”. A cinema or concert ticket is vstupenka. Literally: Mám jízdenku. = “have-I ticket-ACC”.

question: What does “nádraží” mean?
explanation: “nádraží” means “station”. Literally: Kde je nádraží? = “where is station?”.

question: What does “ulice” mean?
explanation: “ulice” means “street”. Literally: Bydlím v téhle ulici. = “live-I in this street”.

question: What does “město” mean?
explanation: “město” means “city / town”. Literally: Praha je velké město. = “Prague is big city”.

question: What does “učitel” mean?
explanation: “učitel” means “teacher (male)”. Female: učitelka. Literally: Můj otec je učitel. = “my father is teacher”.

question: What does “lékař” mean?
explanation: “lékař” means “doctor”. Literally: Jdu k lékaři. = “go-I to doctor”.

question: What does “drahý” mean?
explanation: “drahý” means “expensive”. Literally: To je moc drahé. = “that is too-much expensive”.

question: What does “levný” mean?
explanation: “levný” means “cheap”. Literally: Je to levné. = “is it cheap”.

question: What does “nemocný” mean?
explanation: “nemocný” means “ill”. Literally: Jsem nemocný. = “am-I ill”.

question: What does “mokrý” mean?
explanation: “mokrý” means “wet”. Literally: Ruce jsou mokré. = “hands are wet”.

question: What does “slunečno” mean?
explanation: “slunečno” means “sunny”. Literally: Dnes je slunečno. = “today is sunny”.

question: What does “větrno” mean?
explanation: “větrno” means “windy”. Literally: Dnes je větrno. = “today is windy”.

question: What does “zima” mean?
explanation: “zima” means “cold / winter”. Also means “winter”. Literally: Je zima. = “is cold”.

question: What does “horko” mean?
explanation: “horko” means “hot (weather)”. Literally: Je horko. = “is hot”.

question: What does “někdy” mean?
explanation: “někdy” means “sometimes”. Literally: Někdy chodím do kina. = “sometimes go-I to cinema”.

question: What does “každý den” mean?
explanation: “každý den” means “every day”. Literally: Každý den pracuju. = “every day work-I”.

question: What does “aktuální” mean?
explanation: “aktuální” means “current”. False friend: “actually” is vlastně or ve skutečnosti. Literally: Aktuální cena je nízká. = “current price is low”.

question: What does “Jaké je počasí?” mean?
explanation: “Jaké je počasí?” means “What's the weather like?”. Literally: Jaké je počasí? = “what-kind is weather?”.

question: What does “Prší.” mean?
explanation: “Prší.” means “It's raining.”. Literally: Prší. = “rains”.

question: What does “Sněží.” mean?
explanation: “Sněží.” means “It's snowing.”. Literally: Sněží. = “snows”.

question: What does “Kolik to stojí?” mean?
explanation: “Kolik to stojí?” means “How much does it cost?”. Literally: Kolik to stojí? = “how-much that costs?”.

question: What does “Kde je nádraží?” mean?
explanation: “Kde je nádraží?” means “Where is the station?”. Literally: Kde je nádraží? = “where is station?”.

question: What does “Je mi líto.” mean?
explanation: “Je mi líto.” means “I'm sorry.”. Literally: Je mi líto. = “is to-me sorry”.

question: What does “Nemluvím česky.” mean?
explanation: “Nemluvím česky.” means “I don't speak Czech.”. Literally: Nemluvím česky. = “not-speak-I Czech-in”.

question: What does “Mluvíte anglicky?” mean?
explanation: “Mluvíte anglicky?” means “Do you speak English?”. Literally: Mluvíte anglicky? = “speak-you English-in?”.

question: What does “Mám hlad.” mean?
explanation: “Mám hlad.” means “I'm hungry.”. Literally: Mám hlad. = “have-I hunger”.

question: What does “Mám žízeň.” mean?
explanation: “Mám žízeň.” means “I'm thirsty.”. Literally: Mám žízeň. = “have-I thirst”.

question: What does “Dám si kávu.” mean?
explanation: “Dám si kávu.” means “I'll have a coffee.”. Literally: Dám si kávu. = “give-I myself coffee-ACC”.

question: What does “Vítejte v Praze.” mean?
explanation: “Vítejte v Praze.” means “Welcome to Prague.”. Literally: Vítejte v Praze. = “welcome in Prague-LOC”.

question: Kdybych měl čas, ___ víc. (If I had time, I would read more)
explanation: Conditional: l-participle + bych / bys / by… Literally: Kdybych měl čas, četl bych víc. = “if-I had time, read would-I more”.
phrase: Kdybych měl čas, četl bych víc.

question: Kdybych byl bohatý, ___ si dům. (If I were rich, I'd buy a house)
explanation: Conditional: koupil bych (perfective verb + bych). Literally: Kdybych byl bohatý, koupil bych si dům. = “if-I were rich, bought would-I myself house”.
phrase: Kdybych byl bohatý, koupil bych si dům.

question: Šel ___ s tebou. (I would go with you)
explanation: The conditional auxiliary for “I” is bych. Literally: Šel bych s tebou. = “gone would-I with you”.

question: Mohl ___ mi pomoct? (Could you help me?)
explanation: The conditional auxiliary for “you” (informal) is bys. Literally: Mohl bys mi pomoct? = “could would-you me help?”.

question: Kdybych to ___, nepřišel bych. (If I had known, I wouldn't have come)
explanation: Kdybych + l-participle expresses an unreal condition. Literally: Kdybych to věděl, nepřišel bych. = “if-I it known, not-come would-I”.

question: Muž, ___ tam stojí, je můj učitel. (The man who stands there is my teacher)
explanation: Který agrees with the noun in gender: muž is masculine. Literally: Muž, který tam stojí, je můj učitel. = “man who there stands is my teacher”.
phrase: Muž, který tam stojí, je můj učitel.

question: Kniha, ___ čtu, je dobrá. (The book I'm reading is good)
explanation: Kterou is the feminine accusative: it is the object of čtu. Literally: Kniha, kterou čtu, je dobrá. = “book which read-I is good”.

question: Dům, ___ bydlím, je starý. (The house I live in is old)
explanation: Preposition + relative pronoun: ve kterém (locative). Literally: Dům, ve kterém bydlím, je starý. = “house in which live-I is old”.
phrase: Dům, ve kterém bydlím, je starý.

question: Tady se ___ česky. (Czech is spoken here)
explanation: Reflexive passive: se + 3rd person. Literally: Tady se mluví česky. = “here itself speaks Czech-in”.

question: Tohle auto bylo ___ v Německu. (This car was made in Germany)
explanation: Passive participle + neuter agreement: vyrobeno. Literally: Tohle auto bylo vyrobeno v Německu. = “this car was made in Germany”.
phrase: Tohle auto bylo vyrobeno v Německu.

question: Kniha byla ___ Karlem. (The book was written by Karel)
explanation: Passive: byla + passive participle (agreeing with kniha): napsána. Literally: Kniha byla napsána Karlem. = “book was written Karel-INSTR”.

question: Řekl, že ___ unavený. (He said that he is tired)
explanation: Czech keeps the original tense in reported speech: je. Literally: Řekl, že je unavený. = “said that is tired”.

question: Zeptal se mě, ___ mám čas. (He asked me whether I have time)
explanation: Jestli introduces an indirect yes / no question. Literally: Zeptal se mě, jestli mám čas. = “asked himself me whether have-I time”.
phrase: Zeptal se mě, jestli mám čas.

question: Učím se česky, ___ mohl žít v Praze. (I'm learning Czech so that I can live in Prague)
explanation: Aby + personal ending expresses purpose: abych (I). Literally: Učím se česky, abych mohl žít v Praze. = “learn-I myself Czech so-that-I could live in Prague”.
phrase: Učím se česky, abych mohl žít v Praze.

question: Chci, ___ přišel. (I want you to come)
explanation: Chtít, aby + l-participle: abys (you). Literally: Chci, abys přišel. = “want-I so-that-you came”.

question: Chci ___ pomoct. (I want to help you)
explanation: Pomoct takes the dative: ti. Literally: Chci ti pomoct. = “want-I to-you help”.

question: Vidím ___. (I see you)
explanation: Vidět takes the accusative: tě. Literally: Vidím tě. = “see-I you”.

question: Dal jsem ___ dárek. (I gave him a present)
explanation: Dative of on: mu. Literally: Dal jsem mu dárek. = “gave am-I him present”.

question: Mám ___ rád. (I like him)
explanation: Mít rád takes the accusative: ho. Literally: Mám ho rád. = “have-I him glad”.

question: Zůstanu doma, ___ prší. (I'll stay home because it's raining)
explanation: Protože introduces a reason. Literally: Zůstanu doma, protože prší. = “stay-I at-home because rains”.

question: ___ prší, jdu ven. (Although it's raining, I'm going out)
explanation: Ačkoli (although) introduces a concession. Literally: Ačkoli prší, jdu ven. = “although rains, go-I outside”.

question: Když jsem ___ malý, bydlel jsem v Brně. (When I was little, I lived in Brno)
explanation: Když + past: jsem byl. Literally: Když jsem byl malý, bydlel jsem v Brně. = “when am-I been little, lived am-I in Brno”.
phrase: Když jsem byl malý, bydlel jsem v Brně.

question: Než ___, zavolám ti. (Before I leave, I'll call you)
explanation: Než + perfective present with future meaning. Literally: Než odejdu, zavolám ti. = “before leave-I, call-I you”.

question: Jakmile ___ domů, zavolám ti. (As soon as I get home, I'll call you)
explanation: Jakmile + perfective present with future meaning. Literally: Jakmile přijdu domů, zavolám ti. = “as-soon-as arrive-I home, call-I you”.

question: Včera jsem ___ do Prahy. (Yesterday I travelled to Prague)
explanation: Jet (one trip): jel (past). Literally: Včera jsem jel do Prahy. = “yesterday am-I gone to Prague”.

question: Zítra ___ do Prahy. (Tomorrow I'll travel to Prague)
explanation: The prefix po- gives the future of motion verbs: pojedu. Literally: Zítra pojedu do Prahy. = “tomorrow will-go-I to Prague”.

question: Jedu ___ Prahy. (I'm travelling from Prague)
explanation: Z + genitive = from / out of. Literally: Jedu z Prahy. = “go-I from Prague-GEN”.

question: Bydlím blízko ___. (I live near the park)
explanation: Blízko takes the genitive: parku. Literally: Bydlím blízko parku. = “live-I near park-GEN”.

question: Auto stojí před ___. (The car is parked in front of the house)
explanation: Před (in front of) takes the instrumental: domem. Literally: Auto stojí před domem. = “car stands before house-INSTR”.

question: Díky ___ jsem to zvládl. (Thanks to you I managed it)
explanation: Díky takes the dative: ty → tobě. Literally: Díky tobě jsem to zvládl. = “thanks you-DAT am-I it managed”.

question: Těším se na ___. (I'm looking forward to the holiday)
explanation: Těšit se na + accusative. Literally: Těším se na dovolenou. = “look-forward-I myself on holiday-ACC”.

question: Zajímám se o ___. (I'm interested in music)
explanation: Zajímat se o + accusative. Literally: Zajímám se o hudbu. = “interest-I myself about music-ACC”.

question: What does “nicméně” mean?
explanation: “nicméně” means “nevertheless”. Literally: Bylo pozdě; nicméně jsme šli ven. = “was late; nevertheless went-we outside”.
phrase: Bylo pozdě; nicméně jsme šli ven.

question: What does “navíc” mean?
explanation: “navíc” means “moreover / on top of that”. Literally: Je to drahé, navíc špatné. = “is it expensive, moreover bad”.

question: What does “proto” mean?
explanation: “proto” means “therefore”. Literally: Prší, proto zůstanu doma. = “rains, therefore stay-I at-home”.

question: What does “často” mean?
explanation: “často” means “often”. Literally: Často chodím pěšky. = “often go-I on-foot”.

question: What does “obvykle” mean?
explanation: “obvykle” means “usually”. Literally: Obvykle vstávám v sedm. = “usually get-up-I at seven”.

question: What does “zřídka” mean?
explanation: “zřídka” means “rarely”. Literally: Zřídka jím maso. = “rarely eat-I meat”.

question: What does “práce” mean?
explanation: “práce” means “work / job”. Literally: Mám novou práci. = “have-I new work-ACC”.

question: What does “plat” mean?
explanation: “plat” means “salary”. Literally: Plat je dobrý. = “salary is good”.

question: What does “zkušenost” mean?
explanation: “zkušenost” means “experience”. False friend: “experiment” is pokus. Literally: Mám hodně zkušeností. = “have-I much experiences-GEN”.

question: What does “zklamaný” mean?
explanation: “zklamaný” means “disappointed”. Literally: Jsem zklamaný výsledkem. = “am-I disappointed result-INSTR”.

question: What does “prostředí” mean?
explanation: “prostředí” means “environment / surroundings”. Literally: Musíme chránit životní prostředí. = “must-we protect living environment”.

question: What does “schůzka” mean?
explanation: “schůzka” means “meeting / appointment”. Literally: Zítra mám schůzku. = “tomorrow have-I meeting”.

question: What does “uspět” mean?
explanation: “uspět” means “to succeed”. Literally: Chci uspět. = “want-I succeed”.

question: What does “uvědomit si” mean?
explanation: “uvědomit si” means “to realise”. Literally: Uvědomil jsem si svou chybu. = “realised am-I myself my mistake”.

question: What does “chybět” mean?
explanation: “chybět” means “to be missing / to miss”. The person who is missed is the grammatical subject. Literally: Chybíš mi. = “are-missing-you to-me”.

question: What does “vzpomínat” mean?
explanation: “vzpomínat” means “to remember / to reminisce”. Literally: Rád vzpomínám na dětství. = “gladly recall-I on childhood”.

question: What does “Rád tě vidím.” mean?
explanation: “Rád tě vidím.” means “I'm glad to see you.”. Literally: Rád tě vidím. = “gladly you see-I”.

question: What does “Vítej doma.” mean?
explanation: “Vítej doma.” means “Welcome home.”. Literally: Vítej doma. = “welcome at-home”.

question: What does “Měj se hezky.” mean?
explanation: “Měj se hezky.” means “Take care.”. Literally: Měj se hezky. = “have yourself nicely”.

question: What does “Co si o tom myslíš?” mean?
options: What do you think about it?
explanation: “Co si o tom myslíš?” means “What do you think about it?”. Literally: Co si o tom myslíš? = “what yourself about it think-you?”.

question: What does “Leje jako z konve.” mean?
explanation: “Leje jako z konve.” means “It's pouring.”. Literally: Leje jako z konve. = “pours like from jug”.

question: What does “Pozor!” mean?
explanation: “Pozor!” means “Watch out!”. Literally: Pozor! = “attention”.

question: What does “Možná.” mean?
explanation: “Možná.” means “Maybe.”. Literally: Možná. = “possible”.

question: What does “Bez pochyby.” mean?
explanation: “Bez pochyby.” means “Without a doubt.”. Literally: Bez pochyby. = “without doubt”.

question: What does “Brzy se uzdrav.” mean?
explanation: “Brzy se uzdrav.” means “Get well soon.”. Literally: Brzy se uzdrav. = “soon yourself heal”.

question: What does “Všechno nejlepší!” mean?
explanation: “Všechno nejlepší!” means “Happy birthday! / All the best!”. Literally: Všechno nejlepší! = “everything best”.

question: What does “Šťastný nový rok!” mean?
explanation: “Šťastný nový rok!” means “Happy New Year!”. Literally: Šťastný nový rok! = “happy new year”.

question: What does “Veselé Vánoce!” mean?
explanation: “Veselé Vánoce!” means “Merry Christmas!”. Literally: Veselé Vánoce! = “merry Christmas”.

question: Kdybych se lépe učil, ___ teď lepší práci. (If I had studied better, I'd have a better job now)
explanation: Mixed conditional: past condition + present result with měl bych. Literally: Kdybych se lépe učil, měl bych teď lepší práci. = “if-I myself better studied, had would-I now better work”.
phrase: Kdybych se lépe učil, měl bych teď lepší práci.

question: Každé ráno si ___ kávu. (Every morning I make myself a coffee)
explanation: Imperfective present describes a habit. Literally: Každé ráno si dělám kávu. = “every morning myself make-I coffee”.

question: Včera jsem si ___ kávu a šel jsem do práce. (Yesterday I made myself a coffee and went to work)
explanation: Perfective past: one completed action in a sequence. Literally: Včera jsem si udělal kávu a šel jsem do práce. = “yesterday am-I myself made coffee and gone am-I to work”.
phrase: Včera jsem si udělal kávu a šel jsem do práce.

question: Každý den ___ do práce pěšky. (Every day I walk to work)
explanation: Chodit is the repeated / habitual verb of walking. Literally: Každý den chodím do práce pěšky. = “every day walk-I to work on-foot”.
phrase: Každý den chodím do práce pěšky.

question: Teď ___ do práce. (I'm walking to work now)
explanation: Jít is the single-direction verb of walking. Literally: Teď jdu do práce. = “now go-I to work”.

question: Každý víkend ___ do Brna. (Every weekend I travel to Brno)
explanation: Jezdit is the repeated / habitual verb of travelling. Literally: Každý víkend jezdím do Brna. = “every weekend travel-I to Brno”.

question: V domě není ___. (There's no one in the house)
explanation: Není (there isn't) takes the nominative nikdo. Literally: V domě není nikdo. = “in house is-not nobody”.

question: Neviděl jsem ___. (I saw nobody)
explanation: Negation: nikdo (nobody) becomes nikoho as an object; Czech uses double negation. Literally: Neviděl jsem nikoho. = “not-seen am-I nobody-ACC”.

question: Bojím se ___. (I'm afraid of dogs)
explanation: Bát se takes the genitive: psů. Literally: Bojím se psů. = “fear-I myself dogs-GEN”.

question: Čekám na ___. (I'm waiting for the bus)
explanation: Čekat na + accusative. Literally: Čekám na autobus. = “wait-I on bus-ACC”.

question: Mluvím o ___. (I'm talking about you)
explanation: O + locative: ty → o tobě. Literally: Mluvím o tobě. = “talk-I about you-LOC”.

question: Během ___ jsem se hodně naučil. (During the course I learned a lot)
explanation: Během takes the genitive: kurzu. Literally: Během kurzu jsem se hodně naučil. = “during course-GEN am-I myself much learned”.
phrase: Během kurzu jsem se hodně naučil.

question: Po ___ jsme šli domů. (After the film we went home)
explanation: Po (after) takes the locative: filmu. Literally: Po filmu jsme šli domů. = “after film-LOC are-we gone home”.

question: Před ___ jsem snídal. (Before work I had breakfast)
explanation: Před (before / in front of) takes the instrumental: prací. Literally: Před prací jsem snídal. = “before work-INSTR am-I had-breakfast”.

question: Mezi ___ je rozdíl. (There's a difference between them)
explanation: Mezi takes the instrumental; after a preposition the pronoun gets an n-: nimi. Literally: Mezi nimi je rozdíl. = “between them is difference”.

question: Čím víc se učím, ___ víc umím. (The more I study, the more I know)
explanation: Čím … tím … = the more … the more … Literally: Čím víc se učím, tím víc umím. = “what-by more myself learn-I, that-by more can-I”.
phrase: Čím víc se učím, tím víc umím.

question: Je to ___ než jsem čekal. (It's better than I expected)
explanation: Irregular comparative: dobrý → lepší. Literally: Je to lepší než jsem čekal. = “is it better than am-I expected”.
phrase: Je to lepší než jsem čekal.

question: Je to stejně drahé ___ tamto. (It's as expensive as that)
explanation: Stejně … jako = as … as. Literally: Je to stejně drahé jako tamto. = “is it equally expensive as that”.
phrase: Je to stejně drahé jako tamto.

question: Vzal si ___ klíče. (He took his own keys)
explanation: Svůj is the reflexive possessive: it refers back to the subject. Literally: Vzal si své klíče. = “took himself own keys”.

question: Chtěl ___ vědět, kolik to stojí. (I would like to know how much it costs)
explanation: Conditional for “I”: chtěl bych. Literally: Chtěl bych vědět, kolik to stojí. = “wanted would-I know how-much it costs”.
phrase: Chtěl bych vědět, kolik to stojí.

question: Měl ___ mi zavolat. (You should have called me)
explanation: Měl jsi + infinitive = you should have; měl bys = you should. Literally: Měl jsi mi zavolat. = “had are-you me to-call”.

question: Je ___, že přijde. (It's possible that he'll come)
explanation: Je možné, že … (impersonal) takes the neuter form. Literally: Je možné, že přijde. = “is possible that will-come”.

question: Zdá ___ mi, že máš pravdu. (It seems to me you're right)
explanation: Zdát se (to seem) is reflexive: zdá se mi. Literally: Zdá se mi, že máš pravdu. = “seems itself to-me that have-you truth”.
phrase: Zdá se mi, že máš pravdu.

question: Bylo ___ zima. (I was cold)
explanation: Feelings use the dative: bylo mi zima. Literally: Bylo mi zima. = “was to-me cold”.

question: Kolik ___ je let? (How old are you?)
explanation: Age uses the dative: kolik ti je let? Literally: Kolik ti je let? = “how-many to-you is years?”.

question: Ahoj, ___! (Hi, Petr!)
explanation: The vocative is used when addressing someone: Petr → Petře. Literally: Ahoj, Petře! = “hi, Petr!”.

question: Ahoj, ___! (Hi, mum!)
explanation: Vocative of feminine -a nouns: -o (máma → mámo). Literally: Ahoj, mámo! = “hi, mum!”.

question: Ahoj, ___! (Hi, Honza!)
explanation: Vocative of -a names: -o (Honza → Honzo). Literally: Ahoj, Honzo! = “hi, Honza!”.

question: ___ mi to, prosím. (Tell me, please)
explanation: Imperative of říct: řekni (informal). Literally: Řekni mi to, prosím. = “tell me it, please”.

question: Nebojte ___! (Don't be afraid! (formal))
explanation: Reflexive verbs keep se in the imperative: nebojte se. Literally: Nebojte se! = “not-fear-you yourself!”.

question: Buď tak ___ a zavři okno. (Be so kind and close the window)
explanation: A polite request: buď tak hodný (a woman: hodná). Literally: Buď tak hodný a zavři okno. = “be so good and close window”.
phrase: Buď tak hodný a zavři okno.

question: Mohl ___ mi říct, kolik je hodin? (Could you tell me what time it is? (formal))
explanation: Formal / plural “you”: byste. Literally: Mohl byste mi říct, kolik je hodin? = “could would-you me tell how-much is hours?”.
phrase: Mohl byste mi říct, kolik je hodin?

question: What does “výzva” mean?
explanation: “výzva” means “challenge”. Literally: Je to velká výzva. = “is it big challenge”.

question: What does “pokrok” mean?
explanation: “pokrok” means “progress”. Literally: Děláme velké pokroky. = “make-we big progresses”.

question: What does “rozhodnutí” mean?
explanation: “rozhodnutí” means “decision”. Literally: To je těžké rozhodnutí. = “that is hard decision”.

question: What does “zodpovědnost” mean?
explanation: “zodpovědnost” means “responsibility”. Literally: Mám velkou zodpovědnost. = “have-I big responsibility”.

question: What does “příležitost” mean?
explanation: “příležitost” means “opportunity”. Literally: To je skvělá příležitost. = “that is great opportunity”.

question: What does “názor” mean?
explanation: “názor” means “opinion”. Literally: Mám jiný názor. = “have-I different opinion”.

question: What does “zvyk” mean?
explanation: “zvyk” means “habit / custom”. Literally: To je dobrý zvyk. = “that is good habit”.

question: What does “ekonomika” mean?
explanation: “ekonomika” means “economy”. Literally: Ekonomika roste. = “economy grows”.

question: What does “změna klimatu” mean?
explanation: “změna klimatu” means “climate change”. Literally: Změna klimatu ovlivňuje všechny. = “change climate-GEN affects everyone”.

question: What does “politika” mean?
explanation: “politika” means “politics / policy”. False friend: “police” is policie. Literally: Zajímám se o politiku. = “interest-I myself about politics”.

question: What does “rada” mean?
explanation: “rada” means “advice / council”. Also means “council”. Literally: Potřebuju radu. = “need-I advice-ACC”.

question: What does “podnik” mean?
explanation: “podnik” means “business / enterprise”. Literally: Má malý podnik. = “has-he small business”.

question: What does “vláda” mean?
explanation: “vláda” means “government”. Literally: Vláda sídlí v Praze. = “government sits in Prague”.

question: What does “dosáhnout” mean?
explanation: “dosáhnout” means “to achieve / to reach”. Literally: Chci dosáhnout svého cíle. = “want-I achieve own goal-GEN”.

question: What does “využít” mean?
options: to make use of / to take advantage of
explanation: “využít” means “to make use of / to take advantage of”. Literally: Využijte dobré počasí. = “use good weather”.

question: What does “snažit se” mean?
explanation: “snažit se” means “to try / to strive”. Literally: Snažím se mluvit česky. = “try-I myself speak Czech-in”.

question: What does “Není všechno zlato, co se třpytí.” mean?
options: All that glitters is not gold.
explanation: “Není všechno zlato, co se třpytí.” means “All that glitters is not gold.”. Literally: Není všechno zlato, co se třpytí. = “is-not everything gold what itself glitters”.
phrase: Není všechno zlato, co se třpytí.

question: What does “Pozdě, ale přece.” mean?
explanation: “Pozdě, ale přece.” means “Better late than never.”. Literally: Pozdě, ale přece. = “late, but nevertheless”.

question: What does “Vzít nohy na ramena.” mean?
explanation: “Vzít nohy na ramena.” means “To run away.”. Literally: Vzít nohy na ramena. = “to-take legs on shoulders”.

question: What does “Mít máslo na hlavě.” mean?
explanation: “Mít máslo na hlavě.” means “To have a guilty conscience.”. Literally: Mít máslo na hlavě. = “to-have butter on head”.

question: What does “Být jako na jehlách.” mean?
explanation: “Být jako na jehlách.” means “To be on tenterhooks.”. Literally: Být jako na jehlách. = “to-be like on needles”.

question: What does “Jít s kůží na trh.” mean?
explanation: “Jít s kůží na trh.” means “To put oneself at risk.”. Literally: Jít s kůží na trh. = “to-go with skin to market”.

question: What does “Dostat se z louže pod okap.” mean?
options: To get out of the rain.
To go from the frying pan into the fire.
explanation: “Dostat se z louže pod okap.” means “To go from the frying pan into the fire.”. Literally: Dostat se z louže pod okap. = “to-get oneself from puddle under eaves”.
phrase: Dostat se z louže pod okap.

question: What does “Mít za ušima.” mean?
explanation: “Mít za ušima.” means “To be sly.”. Literally: Mít za ušima. = “to-have behind ears”.

question: What does “Kdo si počká, ten se dočká.” mean?
options: Good things come to those who wait.
explanation: “Kdo si počká, ten se dočká.” means “Good things come to those who wait.”. Literally: Kdo si počká, ten se dočká. = “who himself waits, that-one himself gets-to”.
phrase: Kdo si počká, ten se dočká.

question: What does “Nemáš zač.” mean?
explanation: “Nemáš zač.” means “Don't mention it.”. Literally: Nemáš zač. = “not-have-you for-what”.

question: What does “To nic.” mean?
explanation: “To nic.” means “Never mind.”. Literally: To nic. = “that nothing”.

question: What does “Hodně štěstí!” mean?
explanation: “Hodně štěstí!” means “Good luck!”. Literally: Hodně štěstí! = “much luck-GEN”.
